correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the successor rule from the five XOR generators: the union over pairs of neighbors selects vertices meeting threshold two, and only resting vertices can enter that selection; the next refractory set is the current excited set. An independently written exhaustive ternary-indexed computation checked F^7=F^11 on all 43,046,721 inputs. The first t with F^t=F^(t+4) along each orbit gives its first periodic entry, and the nonzero periodic states were not fixed by F^2. The two columns of shells at t=0 through 7 are (1,65535,3178531,10245950,15448184,10086320,3812880,150400) and (360,5400,53160,0,0,0,0,0). Canonical four-cycles gave 30 basins of 676 and 60 of 644, totaling 58,920 oscillating inputs; the rest basin has 42,987,801. Excited mask 54784 with no refractory vertices reaches rest at step seven and not six, distinguishing F^10 from F^6. Each generator permutation extends linearly by the unique five-term relation; every automorphism fixing zero is determined on the generators because the other ten nonzero vertices are the uniquely identified pair sums. Direct action of all 1,920 maps on cyclic phase tuples recovers the two orbits of sizes 30 and 60 and ties each to its basin size. Four disjoint four-point sets cover the graph in every cycle; XOR zero certifies each affine two-flat, with one common direction or two alternating directions as claimed.
residual_risks: Exact exhaustive computation on this graph and rule only; no formal proof-assistant certification.

value.rationale: The degree-five Clebsch graph is a natural highly symmetric, triangle-free benchmark for the change from one to two excited contacts. The exact comparison establishes a collapse of recurrent periods with survival of two distinct full-vertex wave geometries; the basin and sharp depth data distinguish not just periodic examples but how often and how quickly they are reached. This is a meaningful complete finite classification, not a benchmark for arbitrary graphs or thresholds.
residual_risks: No asymptotic family or general mechanism for the census is claimed.
